title: Priority-zero circuit breaker and tenant communication lane for mixed-deployment canary regressions
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Summary: Create and validate a P0 playbook and automation that combines an emergency circuit-breaker (global and tenant-scoped), a tenant-priority communication lane, and a safe KV/prefix cache reseed flow for regressions discovered during mixed-hosted/dedicated/private canary rollouts. Motivation: Recent canary regressions have surfaced inconsistently across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private customers due to model variant mismatches and stale KV/prefix caches. We need a reproducible, low-latency containment and rollback path that minimizes blast radius, provides transparent customer communications, and ensures cache and state reconciliation during rollbacks or hotpatches.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Playbook documented and reviewed by Eng/PM/Support. 2) Automation implemented for: global circuit-breaker, tenant-scoped circuit-breaker, and tenant isolation API that redirects tenant traffic to a pinned stable variant. 3) KV/prefix cache reseed tool that can run safely in hosted and private environments. 4) Communication templates and escalation tree published and tested. 5) Runbook smoke test executed in staging: simulated canary regression triggers circuit-breaker, reseed flow completes, and tenant traffic returns to stable variant within SLO. 6) Post-test checklist for customer-facing followups added to Console incident workflow.
rollout_steps: 1. Instrumentation: add a lightweight canary-health signal (semantic-quality-score + error-rate) to model rollout controller for mixed deployments.
2. Circuit-breaker knobs: expose global and tenant-scoped kill-switch; default TTL and rate-limited overrides.
3. Tenant-priority lane: create a 3-tier lane (critical-paying, affected-tenants, non-affected) with separate comms templates and SLA promises.
4. KV/prefix reseed tool: build idempotent reseed that accepts tenant scope, model variant, and checkpoint marker; supports dry-run and progress stream.
5. Safe rollback path: implement API to pin tenant to a previous stable model variant and queue a cache invalidation + reseed job.
6. Verification automation: scripted checks for quality metrics, latency regressions, and token-level divergence after reseed/rollback.
7. Runbook staging test: simulate a regression by toggling a canary variant in staging and validate the full flow end-to-end.
8. Documentation and training: host a 90-minute run-through with SRE/Support/SEs and capture FAQs and known limitations.
9. Add observability: dashboard for circuit-breaker state, per-tenant rollback history, KV-seed job progress, and postmortem links.
10. Post-deploy retrospective: collect lessons and iterate on TTLs, thresholds, and comms wording.
Notes: keep the default rollback path conservative to avoid oscillation; avoid mass cache flushes unless necessary.
rollback_playbook:
Immediate steps when a canary quality regression is detected in production:
1) Trigger global or tenant-scoped circuit-breaker depending on scope. Global only if >X% of requests or major semantic failure type.
2) If tenant-scoped: pin affected tenant(s) to last verified model variant via the pin API. Record change in audit log and notify PM/SE.
3) Start KV/prefix cache reseed for pinned tenant(s) with dry-run first if time allows. Use reseed TTL and rate-limit to avoid origin overload.
4) If automated reseed fails or divergence persists, escalate to hotpatch channel: create a hotpatch branch targeting the variant or parameterization causing regression.
5) For Dedicated/Private customers: push an on-prem reseed package and coordinate with customer SRE via the tenant-priority lane.
6) After observed quality metrics recover, clear circuit-breakers in staged fashion: clear non-paying tenants first, then paying, then global.
7) Post-incident: run a reconciliation job to ensure KV caches across replicas and regions are consistent and collect checksum reports.
8) Close loop: send summary comms and schedule one-on-one with any affected enterprise customers within 48 hours.
verification_metrics: Primary: semantic-quality-score (per-tenant baseline delta), fatal-error-rate, 95p latency, token-cost delta. Secondary: KV-cache hit rate, model-variant mismatch count, API error codes by tenant. Recovery-SLO: 90% of affected tenants on stable variant within 30 minutes of circuit-breaker; full reconciliation within 24 hours.
comms_template:
Short customer-facing template: "We detected anomalous model outputs affecting some requests and have enacted a temporary mitigation that routes your traffic to a verified model variant. Our engineers are actively reseeding caches and validating output quality. We will follow up with a technical summary and ETA within 2 hours. Contact your SE or support@redwood.com for urgent questions."
Internal incident channel template: include links to dashboard, pinned variant, KV-reseed job ID, and assigned oncall+liaison.

notes:
Design trade-offs considered: 1) aggressive global circuit-breaker reduces blast radius but increases risk of false positives; we bias toward tenant-scoped first. 2) Full KV flushes are last-resort because of cold-start latency; prefer targeted reseed by tenant/model-checkpoint. 3) For Private deployments, automation should be opt-in; provide signed packages and a remote runbook.
Follow-ups: add audit hooks to Console to show recent pins and reseed jobs; instrument billing impact tracking during rollbacks.
